title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

errors: The notion of 'connected component' of C(ε) is not specified on this page. For the order topology on a dense non-complete order (e.g. Q), components of L−{a,b} would be singletons and the computation fails. It must be meant either for connected (continuum-like) L, or as 'convex component cut out by ε' (the intervals determined by the points of ε). This is an implicit gap, presumably settled elsewhere in the notes.
The computation implicitly assumes C({x,y}) = L−{x,y}, i.e. every triple is in Drop_3(L). Otherwise the components could be smaller than L_{>b}, L_{<b}, ]a,c[. This is not stated here.

Uniqueness of the distinguished element is not checked explicitly, though it is immediate. For a, the pairs {a,b} and {c,a} give ]b,c[ ≠ ∅; for c, the pairs {b,c} and {c,a} give ]a,b[ ≠ ∅. So exactly one point satisfies the criterion. Without density (e.g. Z with consecutive a,b,c) the criterion fails, consistent with the NB.

ideas.what: Recovering the strict betweenness relation of a dense linear order from the separation (component) structure of complements of pairs: the middle point is the one whose two adjacent pairs have disjoint 'opposite' components.
ideas.modern_name: Betweenness relations / reconstruction of order up to reversal from separation or topological data (cut points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical: Pasch, Huntington (betweenness axioms, early 20th c.); order-from-topology characterizations of the line (Eilenberg, Ward, cut-point theory)

ideas.what: Systematic use of density ('divisibilité') as the hypothesis making the intervals ]a,b[, ]b,c[ nonempty and hence the criterion discriminating.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but elementary combinatorial lemma: betweenness is recovered from component data using density. It is a step in Grothendieck's 1986 'réseaux via découpages' program, but the content itself is classical and routine for a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out terms after X_{a,b}, X_{b,c}, X_{c,a} appear to be earlier notations like C_{\{a,b\},c}; the transcription's [-C_{\{a,b,c\}}-] etc. is a reasonable approximation.
'P_2(J)' is written as a script/fraktur P (𝔓_2(J)), consistent with Soc 𝔓_2(L) on p.16.
The third line should read X_{\{c,a\}} = (comp. of C(\{c,a\}) containing b) = ]a,c[, with the opening parenthesis implied by the ditto dashes.
